newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Pub opening hours unlikely to be deregulated.
newsitem.headline: Pub opening hours unlikely to be deregulated.

text.p: The parliamentary committee that is reviewing the liquor laws is unlikely to recommend allowing pubs to stay open later, the committee chairman said on Wednesday.
"I don't think the committee will recommend deregulation (of opening hours)", Charles Flanagan said during the public hearings by the Legislation and Security committee.

He was speaking after the Vintners Federation of Ireland (VFI), which represents some 6,000 publicans in rural Ireland, had called for the extension of closing time to 12.30 a.m. or 1.30 a.m. and for the abolition of Sunday afternoon closing from 2.30 p.m. to 4.30 p.m.
VFI Chairman Tadgh O'Sullivan, said his members did not want the same opening hours as nightclubs, which stay open until three or four a.m.
Deputy Alan Shatter said there was no logical reason why the law should dictate opening and closing times for pubs.
"Parliament, the courts, the police and lawyers should all get out of this area of opening hours and let pubs open when they and their customers want them open", he said.
